gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-sarpanch: Expressive and stencil-cut, Snowburst One spreads wide bridges between tall lowercase letters, while Sarpanch stays compact beneath it. On the page they split the work cleanly.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-stack-sans-notch: Oxanium brings a tall, monoline punch to every heading. Make it small and that big lowercase loses its swagger, while Stack Sans Notch, a plain sans, keeps its curves open.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-sulphur-point: Sulphur Point reads bulky and marker-like, its gaps in a and s clearly open. Under Paprika, whose scattered lowercase fills the line like capitals, a long passage would feel sturdy and steady.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-savate: Snowburst One is all stencil bravado, with tall lowercase held apart by wide bridges. And Savate does the quieter job, its sans-serif curves open and its strokes shifting gently like a soft pencil.
gen-almendra-display-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Almendra Display has an ornate, literary look, with a pronounced x-height and letters that never pinch shut. But Pilcrow Rounded, a plain sans, brings warmth through big counters and strokes like a ballpoint pen.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-pathway-extreme: Funnel Display draws spaghetti-thin strokes of single weight, flat as stencil cuts. Pathway Extreme, a sans with stubby ascenders and a big x-height, can take larger sizes than you would expect beside it.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Flavors is whimsical and towering, its strokes never swelling or thinning, diagonals as hefty as stems. And Noto Sans Warang Citi gives words a solid, block-like feel, so a modest body size is plenty.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-yi: Autour One draws its round letters like spaghetti, each with a clear channel leading in, bold and expressive. Noto Sans Yi, a plain sans, sits deeper in the midsection, so give it a modest size.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Wide glass portholes of lowercase counters make this body text read crisply, with open gaps in c, e, s, and a. Noto Sans Rejang, a sans-serif, gives dark, aggressive Eater something sturdy to lean on.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-devanagari: Noto Sans Devanagari reads compact and modern, its lowercase g opening softly at the bottom. Audiowide handles the futuristic, signage-plain headlines like tiles with wide grout, while Noto Sans Devanagari, a sans-serif, handles the text.
